bad_test_execution_commands_exception_co.correction_reason: Prior count of 330 double-counted each traceback occurrence's two textual mentions of the exception class name (the 'raise BadTestExecutionCommandsException(params)' line and the final 'mutmut.__main__.BadTestExecutionCommandsException: Failed to run pytest...' line). The exact count, verified via grep on the unique final-exception-message line, is 165.
bad_test_execution_commands_exception_co.why_not_recoverable: mutmut 3.7.0's own non-debug per-mutant dispatch loop does not print the mutant's own identifier alongside each test invocation's output -- only an aggregate emoji/counter progress display. The captured run log (this exact, already-completed, non-rerun baseline) therefore does not contain a textual correlation between each BadTestExecutionCommandsException occurrence and the specific mutant identifier being evaluated at that moment. Recovering exact per-occurrence identities would require a NEW debug-mode run, which is not performed here per the instruction not to rerun mutation testing once original evidence was successfully recovered.
bad_test_execution_commands_exception_co.what_is_known: All 165 occurrences are a subset of the 1162 mutants whose raw exit code is 1 ('killed'), specifically an unknown subset representing mutants whose own child-process test invocation crashed via an uncaught BadTestExecutionCommandsException (raised by the installed compatibility shim when a real mutation broke the conftest-imported code path in a way that produced pytest exit code 4) rather than via an ordinary pytest test-assertion failure. Both sub-cases are legitimately classified 'killed' by mutmut's own status_by_exit_code table (exit code 1). No claim is made here about which specific killed mutants belong to which sub-case; this is recorded as a residual evidence gap for the future blind-spot/kill-validity analysis, not resolved in this transaction.
bad_test_execution_commands_exception_co.example_confirmed_instance: A mutation to authority_resolver.py caused a targeted pytest invocation selecting only tests/test_authority_resolver.py's own tests to fail at conftest.py import time (pytest exit code 4); MUTANT_UNDER_TEST was that mutant's own identifier (not 'fail'), so the installed shim correctly did not accept it as a forced-fail success and raised BadTestExecutionCommandsException exactly as unmodified mutmut would.
